page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.i2ne.xlarge is a storage and memory-dense cloud server running on the KVM hypervisor. Powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8163 processor clocked at 2.5 GHz, the instance features 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled to deliver 4 vCPUs. System provisioning includes 32 GB of RAM—providing 8 GB per vCPU core—alongside a bundled 959 GB local SSD storage array and a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps. The underlying processor incorporates 33 MB of L3 cache and supports instruction set extensions including AVX-512, AES cryptography, BMI2, and FMA.

Across standardized benchmarks, the ecs.i2ne.xlarge instance demonstrates lower-tier compute and memory throughput performance relative to contemporary cloud hardware profiles. Stress-ng single-core (1101.89) and multi-core (2923.84) benchmarks place the server in the bottom 25th percentile. Uncached memory read bandwidth (20.18 GB/sec) and write bandwidth (18.64 GB/sec) reflect weak execution bounds. Furthermore, static web serving throughput (2.52 GB/sec) and PassMark database operation tests (1081.7) fall into the bottom 10th percentile.

The instance delivers qualitative cost efficiency for resource configurations that prioritize disk storage capacity and memory density over heavy multi-threaded processing power. Featuring 8 GB of memory per core alongside 959 GB of attached local SSD, ecs.i2ne.xlarge is well structured for localized caching layers, lightweight database deployments, intermediate batch processing, and storage-bound enterprise tasks that do not require high CPU compute throughput.
